The Weierstrass M-Test

One test that settles uniform convergence of a series of functions all at once.

The key is a cap that dominates each term at every point. If the caps themselves sum finitely, the tail shrinks across the whole interval together. So the error band tightens everywhere at once.

For example, think of 📦 box lids covering every item. If the lid sizes add up finitely, nothing can poke out anywhere.

∣fn(x)∣≤Mn ∀x,∑Mn<∞ ⇒ ∑fn converges uniformly|f_n(x)| \le M_n\ \forall x,\quad \sum M_n<\infty\ \Rightarrow\ \sum f_n\ \text{converges uniformly}∣fn​(x)∣≤Mn​ ∀x,∑Mn​<∞ ⇒ ∑fn​ converges uniformly
sup⁡x∣S(x)−SN(x)∣≤∑k>N1k2,N=8: ≈0.1175\sup_x|S(x)-S_N(x)| \le \sum_{k>N}\frac{1}{k^2},\quad N=8:\ \approx 0.1175xsup​∣S(x)−SN​(x)∣≤k>N∑​k21​,N=8: ≈0.1175
